item.title: Make listItems follow cursor pagination
item.brief: Operator request (authenticated, local socket): inventory-client's listItems(transport) must still resolve to every item, in order, by following next_cursor until it is null (or absent), passing the cursor back unchanged. The first request sends no cursor. The inventory-api side of the contract is being implemented in parallel in the inventory-api repository; build against the contract in this brief and tests should use a fake transport, so do not wait on it. Update the README to document the change. Keep `npm test` passing and add tests for multi-page, single-page, and absent next_cursor cases. Commit in this repository; do not push. The shared contract is binding.

pr.body: Approach: listItems loops over GET /items, sending no cursor first, then passing next_cursor back unchanged as query.cursor. It throws if a body has no items array, or if a next_cursor repeats (tracked in a Set, so cycles of any length are caught). Files: client.js, test/client.test.js, README.md. Checks: npm test 9/9 pass; three of the new tests fail on the original code and pass after the change. Assumptions: the server follows the shared contract (cursor is opaque, null on last page); tests use a fake transport, not a real inventory-api. Review: one blocking finding (cursor cycle) fixed in 3acd110 and verified resolved by a delta review. Non-blocking note: the repeated-cursor error text changed from 'same next_cursor twice' to 'already returned'; nothing in the repo matches the old text.
pr.summary: listItems now returns every item across pages. before: only the first page of GET /items, now: all pages in order, following next_cursor until null or absent.

agt_01M88YD36GKETDP8BSRCV04Z5D:1.description: listItems only rejects a next_cursor equal to the immediately previous cursor. A longer cycle (A→B→A) loops forever with growing memory, contrary to the README ("rejects if ... repeats a cursor") and the test name "instead of looping forever". Reproduced: still looping after 6 requests. Fix by tracking a Set of seen cursors and adding an A→B→A test.

risk.why: Changes listItems behaviour in one client function: it now issues several GET /items requests and returns all items. getItem and lowStock are unchanged. Tests cover multi-page, single-page, absent next_cursor, cursor passthrough, missing items array and repeated-cursor cycles, all with a fake transport only. Both reviewers agree on medium; one earlier delta review rated it low, but medium is kept because the rubric says pick the higher level when in doubt.

item.title: Add cursor pagination to GET /items
item.brief: Operator request (authenticated, local socket): GET /items in inventory-api returns every item in one response, which no longer scales. Add cursor pagination. Query params: limit (integer 1..100, default 20) and cursor (opaque string from a previous response). Body becomes {"items": [...], "next_cursor": <string or null>}; items stay ordered by id; next_cursor is null on the last page. Invalid limit or cursor -> status 400 with body {"error": "..."}. Update the README to document the change. Keep `python3 -m unittest` passing and add tests for paging, limit bounds, cursor validity and the last page. Commit in this repository with the operator's git identity already configured; do not push. The shared contract is binding.

evidence.caption: Before (23044eb): default GET /items returns all items, with no next_cursor and limit ignored
After: invalid limit and cursor return 400 with {error}; overlong input returns 400 with no exception

pr.body: Approach: keyset paging on id. The cursor is base64url of the last returned id; the next page is ids greater than it. limit and cursor are parsed in parse_limit and parse_cursor, which raise BadParameter, mapped to 400 at the list_items boundary. Length guards run before int() so overlong digit strings return 400 rather than raising ValueError. Key files: api.py, test_api.py, README.md. Checks: python3 -m unittest, 10 tests OK; py_compile OK; pyflakes not installed. Review fix: overlong digit inputs (Review-Fix trailers on b471ce0). Assumptions: cursors are opaque to clients; the length guard rejects zero-padded limits longer than 3 digits. Limits: the paging-walk test covers only limit=10; get_item's pre-existing int() issue is untouched.
pr.summary: GET /items: pages of limit (1..100, default 20) with opaque cursor. before: all items, no next_cursor. now: {items, next_cursor}, next_cursor null on last page; invalid limit/cursor -> 400 {error}. Breaking for callers expecting all items.
pr.title: Add cursor pagination to GET /items

agt_01M88YDZXQK42E8S54P22VBFNG:1.description: parse_limit calls int(raw) on any all-ASCII-digit string. Python 3.14 caps int-from-str at 4300 digits, so limit=<5000 digits> raises an uncaught ValueError from handle() instead of returning 400 with the documented limit error. Reproduced: limit='9'*5000 -> ValueError. The fix is to bound the length of raw or catch ValueError and raise BadParameter. at api.py:53

agt_01M88YDZXQK42E8S54P22VBFNG:2.description: parse_cursor calls int(decoded) outside the try block. A cursor that base64-decodes to more than 4300 ASCII digits raises an uncaught ValueError instead of the documented 400 'cursor is not valid'. Reproduced: cursor=base64('9'*5000) -> ValueError. Move the int conversion into the validation that raises BadParameter, or bound the length first. at api.py:71

agt_01M88YDZXQK42E8S54P22VBFNG:3.description: Tests do not cover oversized numeric input, non-ASCII input (e.g. cursor='é', limit with non-ASCII digits), or a cursor that decodes to a non-digit or non-UTF-8 payload beyond the listed cases. That gap is how the uncaught ValueError above went unnoticed. Add cases for limit and cursor values of more than 4300 digits, expecting 400. at test_api.py:27

agt_01M88YDZXQK42E8S54P22VBFNG:4.description: parse_cursor accepts non-canonical encodings of the same id, such as base64('01') for id 1, and leading zeros in limit are accepted (limit='0100' -> 100). Harmless for the contract, but worth noting if cursors are ever compared as strings. at api.py:71

agt_01M88YE5N0R546Y8745W11K5ZK:1.description: parse_limit calls int(raw) on untrusted input outside any error handling. A digit string longer than 4300 characters (e.g. limit='1'*5000) raises ValueError ('Exceeds the limit (4300 digits) for integer string conversion') and escapes handle() instead of returning 400 {"error": ...} as documented. Fix: reject overly long digit strings (e.g. len(raw) > 3 before int) or wrap the conversion and raise

agt_01M88YE5N0R546Y8745W11K5ZK:2.description: parse_cursor calls int(decoded) outside the try block. A valid-base64 cursor that decodes to more than 4300 digits (e.g. base64 of b'9'*5000) raises an uncaught ValueError instead of 400 'cursor is not valid'. Fix: bound the decoded length or move the conversion under the same BadParameter handling. at api.py:71

agt_01M88YE5N0R546Y8745W11K5ZK:3.description: Paging-walk test uses only limit=10. Limits 1, 7, 20, 57 and 100 were checked manually in a temp copy and all return ids 1..57 exactly once in order, but they are not covered by tests. Also no test covers the oversized-digit inputs above. at test_api.py:32

agt_01M88YE5N0R546Y8745W11K5ZK:4.description: Pre-existing: get_item does int(raw_id) after isdigit(), so a path id with more than 4300 digits also raises an uncaught ValueError. Not introduced by this commit. at api.py:78

agt_01M88YEBR3TBPGAFNFWSE8ZGXA:1.description: parse_limit calls int(raw) on an all-ASCII-digit string with no length guard. A string of more than 4300 digits (e.g. limit='9'*5000) raises an uncaught ValueError ('Exceeds the limit (4300 digits)') that escapes handle() instead of the documented 400. Reproduced on Python 3.14.7. at api.py:53

agt_01M88YEBR3TBPGAFNFWSE8ZGXA:2.description: parse_cursor calls int(decoded) with no length guard. A cursor whose base64 decodes to more than 4300 digits (e.g. base64 of '9'*5000) raises an uncaught ValueError instead of the documented 400 'cursor is not valid'. Reproduced on Python 3.14.7. at api.py:71

agt_01M88YEBR3TBPGAFNFWSE8ZGXA:3.description: No test covers overlong digit strings for limit or cursor, so the uncaught-exception path above is untested. test_limit_bounds and test_invalid_cursor_is_400 should add cases such as '9'*5000 and a base64 of 5000 digits, expecting 400. at test_api.py:27

agt_01M88YEBR3TBPGAFNFWSE8ZGXA:4.description: Pre-existing, outside this diff: get_item uses str.isdigit(), which accepts '²' (superscript two), then int() raises an uncaught ValueError, so GET /items/² crashes instead of returning 400. Overlong id strings hit the same int() limit. Not introduced by this range, so non-blocking. at api.py:75

agt_01M88YGT70W310XV5KBXWMB2VH:2.description: Length guard rejects zero-padded limits by digit count, not value: limit '0100' (value 100, within 1..100) returns 400 while '010' returns 200. Acceptable as a conservative choice, but inconsistent with the contract's numeric range and should be documented or normalized. at api.py:56

risk.why: Changes the response of an existing API endpoint: the default page size of 20 truncates responses for callers expecting every item, and the body gained next_cursor. Contract-mandated. Touches only api.py, test_api.py and README.md; no persistence, auth or concurrency.
